artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Giordano stages Ovid's Sicilian triangle at the fatal instant: Galatea with Acis while Polyphemus looms with the rock that will crush him.

artworks.title: Acis and Galatea
artworks.description: Claude's golden pastoral: the lovers at ease before the Cyclops' jealousy — Sicilian idyll as classical landscape.

artworks.title: Acis, Galatea, and Polyphemus
artworks.description: Perrier's Louvre canvas: Galatea and Acis slip away while Polyphemus watches from the rocks — the boulder already waiting.

artworks.title: Polyphemus and Galatea (Boscotrecase)
artworks.description: Third-Style fresco from Boscotrecase: Polyphemus among his flock as Galatea rides a dolphin — the Sicilian romance before Ovid.

music.title: Acis and Galatea
music.description: Handel's pastoral masque stages the Sicilian shepherd crushed by Polyphemus — Acis as English Baroque's favourite rustic martyr.

popCulture.title: Acis and Galatea (mythology)
popCulture.description: The shepherd crushed by Polyphemus' rock — Galatea's love becomes a Sicilian river in Ovid's telling.
